reason: The text describes the plague of the firstborn, which indiscriminately harms all Egyptians—both elite and common people alike. All firstborn die 'from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sits on his throne to the firstborn of the servant girl' (Exodus 12:29). This is divine judgment affecting all classes equally, not an instance of the elite attempting to harm regular people. While Pharaoh's prior enslavement of the Israelites could be characterized as elite oppression of regular people, the text fragment itself depicts universal suffering from plague rather than targeted harm by one group against another.
